ei.subject: 영어Ⅰ
ei.title: The ABCs of Stocks and Stock Markets

fullPassage: A bull market is a rising stock market situation in which economic conditions are ① <u>favorable</u> to investors. They include high employment rates, GDP increases, and other ② <u>positive</u> economic indicators. In a bull market, investors often believe in the market's present and future performance. As such, they increase their stock purchases. Like a standing bear having lowered its front legs, a bear market implies a ③ <u>decline</u> in stock values. Factors like low GDP growth, rising unemployment, and low wages are possible conditions for a bear market. In difficult economic situations, investors frequently have ④ <u>negative</u> views of the stock market, which may lead them to ⑤ <u>maintain</u> their stocks.

questions.passage: Today, we're going to provide you with an overview of stocks and stock markets, <u>ⓐ enabling</u> you to gain insight into the economy. A stock is a partial share of ownership in a company. To put it simply, <u>ⓑ owning</u> one stock is like <u>ⓒ having</u> a slice of the company's pie. However, companies hold stockholder meetings <u>ⓓ seeking</u> the opinions of major stockholders when they make important decisions. The stock market is very important for companies because it can provide them with the money they need <u>ⓔ to grow</u> and expand.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 고르시오.

det.korean: 회사는 주주들의 의견을 구하기 위해 주주총회를 개최한다. seeking은 동시동작이 아니라 목적의 의미이므로 to seek으로 고쳐야 합니다.
det.analysis: 원문: companies hold stockholder meetings seeking the opinions
det.tip: 어법 유형 — 지문을 꼼꼼히 읽고 정답을 찾으세요.

questions.passage: When a company is listed on the stock market, individuals or organizations can buy shares. The more successful a business is, the more people will see the potential value of the company and start (B) <u>[buying / to buy]</u> its stocks. As demand for the stocks increases, so (C) <u>[does / is]</u> the stock price.

det.korean: 자금 조달을 쉽게 만든다. 주식을 사기 시작한다. 주가도 마찬가지로 오른다.

Generally, it would be smart to invest in something <u>ⓓ that</u> interests you.

When a company is listed on the stock market, individuals or organizations that believe in the company's bright future can buy shares and become partial owners of the company. questions.passage: Just like other transactions, the prices of stocks are decided by the law of supply and demand. The more successful a business is, the more people will see the potential value of the company and start buying its stocks. Companies are constantly under the influence of market factors such as raw material prices, advances in production technology, and labor costs. Additionally, investors may be concerned about a company's leadership or reputation. Nowadays, more and more people are starting to support companies that prioritize public values such as business transparency, environmental friendliness, and social justice. All these variables can cause daily changes in stock prices in the stock market.

Since the market constantly fluctuates, there is a risk of loss and debt. Always remember to do your research, stay informed about the companies you invest in, and be mindful of your risk tolerance.
